checks.name: Level payment equals the textbook formula AND a bisection on the balance (400 random loans incl. 0% rate, 12-480 months)
Balance today after m paid payments equals month-by-month recurrence (300 random owned loans)
Portfolio debt series for a loan with extra payments equals the reference balance every month, and is 0 after payoff (60 random)
Months to pay off (payoffN) with extra payments equals month-by-month simulation (300 random incl. never-pays-off cases)

Interest-only: payment = balance x rate/12, balance never falls without extra, extra reduces it, 0% IO is a free payment of 0; no default-plan interest-only loan outlives its term (balloon not modeled)
FHA / 203(k): loan = (price + financed rehab) x (1 - down) x (1 + 1.75% upfront premium); down is 3.5% of price + rehab; cash at closing excludes rehab
FHA annual premium is charged on the remaining balance EXCLUDING the financed upfront premium (24 CFR 203.284), so it falls as the loan is paid down
checks.detail: mip at month 240: engine 63.00 vs declining-balance 63.00

checks.name: Closing costs are a % of PRICE (not loan); cash needed at closing = down payment + closing costs; custom % overrides the global default
FHA premium rates match HUD (upfront 1.75%; annual 0.55% for >95% LTV, base loan <= $726,200, term > 15 yrs) and Limited 203(k) cap $75,000
noiOf equals the reference NOI (vacancy off rent, management on collected rent, repairs % of price, fixed costs) for 300 random homes and commercial; business NOI is the owner profit
view(): cash flow = NOI - payment - mortgage insurance; cap rate = 12*NOI/price; price multiple = price/(12*NOI); DSCR basis (NOI / P+MIP) consistent (200 random)
Portfolio NOI series = sum of asset NOI x growth factor: income and costs grow with the asset growth rate (checked at months 0, 60, 180 on 40 random assets)
Default vacancy vs Census HVS rental vacancy (US 7.1% in 2025, 7.4% in 2026 YTD, 8.2% avg 2000-2025): default must be >= 7% or the UI must name the Census figure and say why lower
checks.detail: default vac 5%; glossary mentions Census: true

checks.name: Default management fee 8% and repairs 1%/yr are disclosed as rule-of-thumb assumptions (no fetched source; NARPM / NRC figures were not reachable)

Commercial rows state that rent is net of what tenants reimburse (tax/insurance/CAM): default commercial property tax + insurance are well below typical 1%+ of value, so the UI must say expense lines are net of NNN pass-throughs
checks.detail: tax+insurance = 0.70-0.70% of price per year; disclosed true

checks.name: Default portfolio cap rates and price multiples fall in the bands of the grader benchmark files (bench-cre.json / bench-business.json; secondary sources, flagged unverified there)

Months until the credit line (locMonths) equals an independent month-by-month simulation where the appraisal cut is taken off the VALUE (cap x value x (1 - cut) - balance - liens), incl. saved cash flow (120 random)
extraFor: the extra payment returned reaches the target month and 1 dollar less does not (40 random; null only when infeasible)
After the credit-line draw the combined loan (balance + other liens + draw) never exceeds cap x value x (1 - appraisal cut) (cltvAtLoc, 100 random)

Default max combined loan-to-value (cap) does not exceed the 85% supervisory ceiling for improved property incl. non-owner-occupied 1-4 family (12 CFR 365 App. A); default credit-line rate sits between prime (7.00%, Fed H.15) and prime + 3.5
A credit line behind a BUSINESS (not real estate, no supervisory 85% limit) is disclosed as unrealistic at the same cap, or capped lower
Credit-line interest: draw x line rate / 12 per month from the month the line is drawn, none before; the draw shows as debt then; draw = cash needed minus saved cash flow
Saved cash flow = max(0, NOI - payment - MIP), capped at the cash needed, and what is saved is deducted from liquid cash when the target closes (no double count)
DTI at month 0 equals the reference (75% of gross rent minus the property payment: a positive net adds to income, a negative net adds to debts; plus co-signer and job income; 80 random portfolios)

DTI limit default 43% and rental haircut 75% are consistent with CFPB (43% was the old General QM cap, now replaced by price-based test) and the UI says lenders vary (up to ~50%); wording must not present 43% as a current legal rule
checks.detail: Your monthly debt payments divided by the monthly income a lender counts. Limits vary by loan and lender, often 43% to 50% at most. This app does not add your o

checks.name: DTI includes the borrower's OWN housing payment (rent or mortgage) as a lender would, or the UI discloses that it does not

Every purchase in the default plan meets its lender's minimum DSCR at closing (SBA 7(a)/504 >= 1.15, bank loans >= 1.25 as the app states, DSCR loan >= 1.2 as the app states, bridge and seller notes >= 1.0)
No asset in the default plan cash-flows negative at its own purchase (owner requirement: homes never negative; commercial and businesses must at least pay their own loan)
Debt-to-income in the default plan stays at or under the limit at every month (no purchase that a lender would decline on DTI)
checks.detail: peak DTI 0.9% at month 26 vs limit 43

checks.name: Default plan loan rules: each SBA 7(a) <= $5M and the 7(a) balances outstanding at once <= $5M (conservative reading: SBA aggregates a borrower and affiliates), 504 only for owner-occupied property, bank real-estate loans <= 85% LTV, no seller note above 50% of price
Conventional 30-yr investor: 360 months, rate between PMMS 30-yr (7.18%) and PMMS + 1.0 (investor price adjustment), down >= 15%
Conventional 15-yr: 180 months, rate between PMMS 15-yr (6.57%) and +1.0, down >= 15%
FHA 30-yr: 3.5% down, upfront 1.75%, annual 0.55%, owner-occupied flag, rate <= PMMS 30-yr
203(k): 3.5% down, same premiums, finances rehab, owner-occupied, Limited cap $75,000 stated, default rehab within it
DSCR investor loan: 30-yr, down 20-25%, rate above the conventional investor rate (7.18% PMMS + premium)
Cash purchase (home): 100% down, 0% rate, no loan
Commercial bank 25-yr: 300 months, down 20-35% (65-80% LTV; supervisory limit 85%), rate near prime (7.00%) +0 to +1.5
SBA 504: 25-yr real estate term allowed (10/20/25), down payment 10% standard, max debenture $5.5M, owner-occupancy stated
Bridge loan: interest-only, short term (<= 5 yrs), rate above prime (>= 8.5%)
Seller financing (commercial): negotiated; rate not below the 30-yr mortgage rate minus 2 pts, term <= 30 yrs, preset note says terms vary and typical share is partial
SBA 7(a) business: <= 10-year term for business acquisition (25 for real estate), max loan $5M stated, rate <= prime + 3.0 (10.00%) for loans over $350k, min 10% injection
Bank term loan (business): 5-10 yr term, rate above prime, down >= 20%
Seller note (business): <= 10-yr term, note says the seller finances only part of the price and the share is limited
Cash purchase (business): 100% down, 0% rate
Value at month k = price x (1+g)^(k/12) (compound, months/12); after an improvement the appraisal replaces it and then compounds from completion (60 random)
Living costs and manager pay inflate monthly-compounded by (1+inflation)^(t/12); job pay raises in whole years; income and costs share the same time base (nominal dollars, plan month t)

Default home appreciation (4%/yr; rent and costs grow with value) sits inside the observed range: FHFA purchase-only US HPI 1991-2026 grew 4.32%/yr, 20-year rolling windows 2.75%-4.38% (median 3.56%). The UI must state the FHFA figure, that rent and costs grow with value, and that dollars are nominal
checks.detail: home growth 4 vs FHFA 20y range 2.75-4.38; disclosed with FHFA figure: true

checks.name: Commercial growth defaults (4.5%/yr) are no higher than the best 20-year FHFA home-price window plus 0.25 pt, or the UI says commercial growth is an assumption with no fetched benchmark
checks.detail: informational (weight 0): commercial growth 4.5%; no fetched commercial price index (NCREIF/CBRE blocked)

checks.name: Stress-test and totals use the same time base: category strip "lasts" costs are grown to the plan-end month like the income they offset (engine.stress exists and scales fixed costs by the growth factor)
Default business growth (7.5%/yr for 28 yrs) is above the long-run growth of the U.S. economy (~4% nominal); this must be disclosed as an assumption, not a forecast
checks.detail: max business growth 9%; glossary compares with economy growth: true

checks.name: Income tax estimate (estTaxPct) equals the 2026 single-filer reference: standard deduction $16,100, brackets 10% to 12,400 ... 37% over 640,600, Social Security 6.2% to $184,500, Medicare 1.45% (13 incomes)
Sale tax = max(0, sale price x (1 - selling cost) - original price - improvements) x sales-tax % (checked on 30 random sells)
Default sale-tax 25% sits in the federal range for a sale: 15-20% long-term capital gain + 3.8% NIIT (18.8-23.8%), unrecaptured depreciation up to 25%; text states these, and notes state tax
checks.detail: The tax owed on the profit from a sale. Profit on something held under a year is usually taxed like regular income. Longer-held gains are taxed federally at 15% or 20%, plus 3.8% for high earners, and

checks.name: Flat tax on portfolio income (default 20%) understates federal rates on large profits (32-37% over ~$200k, + 3.8% NIIT; IRS 2026 brackets): the glossary must say so
Depreciation (27.5 yrs residential, 39 yrs non-residential; IRS Pub. 946) is not modeled; the UI must say so (it lowers taxable income and creates recapture on sale)
checks.detail: depreciation mentioned in both glossary entries: true

checks.name: Selling-cost defaults (home 6%, commercial 5%, business 8%) are disclosed as typical ranges
checks.detail: Agent or broker fees and closing costs when you sell. Homes are often 5% to 7%. Commercial properties and businesses var

checks.name: Business price multiples by size in the default plan: <$1.5M 2.0-3.8x, $1.5-5M 2.5-5.2x, >$5M 3.5-7x of owner profit (bench-business.json: BizBuySell avg ~2.6-2.7x SDE for small deals; larger deals higher; sources unverified, flagged)
Manager cost for businesses you do not run = max(0, businesses held - run yourself) x monthly pay, inflated, only while the business is held and not sold or merged into another (random 30)
Hours check: weekly hours = job hours (while the job runs) + min(run yourself, businesses held) x hours per business; flagged tight above 70 (random 30)
Default plan: 28-year growth of 7.5%/yr per business is disclosed as an optimistic assumption in the UI, and the finance sim does not need outside capital
Sell / merge: sale proceeds = value x (1 - selling cost) - balance - liens - line draw; merge lift scales value and income by (1 + lift) from the merge month (random 20)
Default plan: list order = buy order (owned first, then non-decreasing purchase months), every asset gets a purchase month inside the plan, no unfunded asset
Combined portfolio total equals the sum of the rows at 12 months across the plan (net worth, value, debt, cash flow, payments)
Funding chain: every credit-line funder closes the target exactly funder-purchase + months-to-line; the target buys at the earliest such month; no cycles
Cash recycling: sale proceeds go to cash, purchases use cash before outside money; cash never negative; outside draws only for the shortfall (random 25)

Stress test ("lasts"): the ~45% biggest earners fail (rent gone, fixed costs and loan payments still due), everything at plan-end values: re-derived independently on 30 random category sets, including that fixed costs have grown with the asset
Glossary numbers agree with sources: FHA 1.75% + 0.55% (HUD), Limited 203(k) $75,000 (ML 2024-13), SBA 7(a) $5M and 504 $5.5M (SBA.gov), DSCR 1.2/1.25 wording, 43% DTI wording

The Assumptions page carries a "how the numbers are built" note: nominal dollars, rent and costs grow with value, payments are fixed, DTI excludes own housing, credit lines assume 85% cap, no depreciation, flat tax rates

Units and bases are stated (net worth definition says it is before selling costs/taxes and excludes personal savings): yearly inputs say "/ yr", monthly say "/ mo"; DTI limit, vacancy, management are percentages of the right base (vacancy and management of rent; repairs of value per year)
Preset notes that state a number or rule match LOANS fields (FHA/203(k)/SBA caps, owner-occupancy, interest-only) and the sellerb/sellerc notes say the share seller-financed is partial and negotiable
checks.detail: The seller finances part of the price. This preset has the seller carry 80%, which is aggressive; sellers usually carry 10% to 50%.
